episode_title: Empowering Builders Through AI with Meirav Oren of Versatile

real_qa.q: How does Versatile's smart hook device collect data from construction cranes to measure job site processes?
real_qa.r: Versatile uses a hardware device that is a hook under the hook—a lifting accessory that contains everything in a cell phone plus a load cell that tells the weight. With all those sensors giving data from the exact same point at regular intervals, you can learn what load the crane is picking, what process it's involved in, and how long things really take. The device looks tiny on the crane but gigantic on the ground, and it hangs off the crane to collect data without being intrusive to workflows.
real_qa.requete: Versatile smart hook construction crane data collection

real_qa.q: What is the key difference between how Versatile measures construction work versus visual progress tracking methods?
real_qa.r: Versatile measures process, not progress. Visual tracking tells you if something was installed or not, but Versatile tells you how long it took to install it, where materials came from, how long it took to get them there, and what took so long to get stuff off the truck. You can understand stripping and installation on formwork at a level of detail that visual aids alone cannot provide. This process-level detail is what enables actionable insights.
real_qa.requete: Versatile construction process measurement vs progress tracking

real_qa.q: How much funding has Versatile raised despite starting as a bootstrapped hardware-enabled SaaS company?
real_qa.r: Versatile raised over 109 million dollars after bootstrapping and facing more no's than most founders would dare to hear. The first money Versatile ever received was from winning the Mass Challenge accelerator, which was put toward the first trip to the target market and filing a patent, with no money going into the founder's paycheck initially.

real_qa.q: What specific process improvements has Versatile's data revealed for construction customers, such as Internal Construction?
real_qa.r: Internal Construction, an enterprise customer, published a video showing that understanding they should pre-stage materials saved them 90 seconds per lift times thousands of lifts. Another case showed a customer realized they had started a new practice that was slowing them down by 8 minutes per lift times 512 lifts, costing them days on end, without anyone knowing it using a stopwatch.
real_qa.requete: Versatile Internal Construction case study savings per lift

real_qa.q: Why did Versatile focus specifically on cranes rather than other construction equipment as its data collection point?
real_qa.r: Versatile focused on cranes because they believe the crane sees 70 to 80 percent of construction processes, either directly through installing materials and elements or indirectly through moving them. The crane is the pacemaker and storyteller of what happens on a job site. Versatile only takes on jobs where the crane plays a pivotal role and is the unbelievable storyteller of the story they want to tell to the people they serve.
real_qa.requete: why Versatile chose cranes for construction data collection

real_qa.q: What is Versatile's approach to AI analysis of construction data rather than making predictive or prescriptive recommendations?
real_qa.r: Versatile does not yet use AI to be predictive or prescriptive. Meirav Oren argues the construction industry is not necessarily ready for that level of AI trust. Instead, Versatile provides factual measurements—such as this task takes nine minutes normally but took 48 yesterday—and turns customer attention to a single process that took much longer, letting superintendents use their own judgment. The company gives information and lets experienced builders decide what to do.

guest.bio_context: Meirav Oren spent time at Intel, which she describes as one of the best business schools and a company with wonderful mentors. She grew up in a construction family with her father as a general contractor and her brother as a project manager in construction. A traumatic incident where her brother's project lost a worker prompted her to start Versatile, aiming to bring data-driven control to the construction industry.
